title: M3XU: Achieving High-Precision and Complex Matrix Multiplication with Low-Precision MXUs
problem: Low-precision matrix processing units (MXUs) designed for AI/ML workloads are underutilized when executing applications requiring IEEE 754 single-precision or complex floating-point matrix operations. Existing MXUs cannot efficiently support high-precision scientific and technical computing workloads.
motivation: Strong demand exists for high-performance matrix operations on standard and complex floating-point numbers in non-AI/ML scientific computing, but current low-precision MXUs remain idle or underutilized outside their target domains.
method: M3XU extends existing MXUs through a multi-step computational approach to support IEEE 754 single-precision and complex 32-bit floating-point operations without requiring additional costly multipliers. The design reuses existing MXU infrastructure and enables seamless integration into current systems while maintaining compatibility with existing memory subsystems, requiring no programmer modifications.
key_novelty: Enabling low-precision MXUs to handle high-precision and complex floating-point matrix operations through a multi-step approach without additional multiplier hardware.
contributions: Multi-mode MXU architecture supporting both AI/ML and high-precision complex floating-point matrix operations
Seamless system integration method enabling MXU extensions without programmer effort or memory subsystem changes
3.64x speedup for 32-bit matrix multiplications and 3.51x speedup for complex number operations versus conventional vector processing units
Full-system validation through emulation and hardware synthesis

metrics.speedup: 3.64x for 32-bit matrix multiplications, 3.51x for complex operations

primary_theme: Multi-mode matrix acceleration for scientific computing
